## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/tmp/codex-home/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

<multi_agent_mode>Any earlier instruction enabling proactive multi-agent delegation no longer applies. Do not spawn sub-agents unless the user or applicable AGENTS.md/skill instructions explicitly ask for sub-agents, delegation, or parallel agent work.</multi_agent_mode>

# Diagnose and repair the staged experiment

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a snapshot you may repair: inspect its
source, effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic,
logs, tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an
unusual setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed
behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health.

## Your job

If you find a defect, fix it in the staged workspace at `/workspace`. **Do not
launch training.** Do not start the experiment, in the foreground or
background, and do not use `nohup`, `&`, `tmux`, `screen`, or any detach
mechanism. The system runs the experiment itself after you finish (see below);
anything you launch is wasted and scores nothing. Cheap, non-training checks
are fine.

**Do not use the network.** Do not fetch code, documentation, packages,
or any other material from outside the staged workspace — diagnose and
repair using only what is staged locally.

When you are done, submit a report at `/workspace/report.md`. It must
summarize:

1. **Verdict** — healthy or unhealthy, with the evidence that decides it.
2. **Root cause** — the defect you found, and the evidence in the workspace
   (logs, metrics, code) that connects it to the observed behavior.
3. **Changes** — every file you changed and what you changed in it.
4. **Expected effect** — which metric the fix should move and in which
   direction.

A missing or empty `/workspace/report.md` scores 0.

## What the system will run

After you submit the report, the system deletes everything under
`$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`, then re-runs the experiment in your
repaired workspace as a foreground process, using the launch script:

```text
examples/search-r1/run_qwen2.5_3B.sh
```

with this environment:

```text
LOG_DIR=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs
WANDB_MODE=offline
WANDB_DIR=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs
```

The effective run must use:

- HF checkpoint `/workspace/Qwen2.5-3B`
- Megatron torch_dist reference `/workspace/Qwen2.5-3B_torch_dist`
- train data `/workspace/nq_hotpotqa_train/train.parquet`
- validation data `/workspace/nq_hotpotqa_train/test.parquet`
- `--num-rollout 100`
- `--eval-interval 10`
- local retrieval server `http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve`

**Make sure your repaired launch script actually produces that run.** The
graded rerun passes no budget or environment overrides — whatever the script
bakes into the training invocation is what runs, and a run that exceeds its
time budget scores 0.

Four more traps specific to this task:

- **Log placement is your script's job.** The launch script builds the Ray
  runtime-env JSON itself and only propagates a few variables into the
  training process — `WANDB_DIR` set in the environment does **not** reach it.
  Your repaired script must itself write the training log and the offline
  W&B data under `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs` (offline W&B below
  `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs/wandb`), or the grader will find no
  metrics to grade.
- **The W&B key.** The script passes `--wandb-key ${WANDB_API_KEY}` unquoted;
  offline mode gets a harmless local placeholder from the environment, so the
  script must not choke when it is a placeholder rather than a real key.
- **Read-only scoring assets.** `examples/search-r1/qa_em_format.py` (the
  exact-match scorer the launch script wires as the custom reward manager),
  `examples/search-r1/local_dense_retriever/` (the retrieval server), and the
  staged datasets under `nq_hotpotqa_train/` are graded read-only: after the
  rerun the verifier hashes them, and any modification, replacement, or
  deletion scores 0 no matter what the metrics say. Any repair belongs in the
  staged workspace outside these protected assets.
- **The launch script's scoring and eval wiring is fixed.** The script must
  keep wiring the run exactly as staged: the custom generate/reward-manager
  paths (`generate_with_search.generate` /
  `generate_with_search.reward_func`), the eval on `nq_test` over the staged
  `test.parquet` with its `[0:3000]` slice, `--eval-interval 10`, and
  `--n-samples-per-eval-prompt 1`. The verifier checks these after the rerun;
  repointing the scorer, swapping the eval dataset, or resampling evals scores
  0 no matter what the metrics say.

A task-specific grading script then reads **only this fresh run's** files
under `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs` and scores the key metrics; logs
written anywhere else are ignored. Do not copy, edit, or fabricate log
metrics. Otherwise the run is scored 0.

I’ll inspect the staged source, launch path, configuration, data and evaluation artifacts, then trace the observed metrics back to the implementation. I’ll make only the necessary repairs, run cheap static checks, and write the required report without launching training.

#!/bin/bash

# Kill leftover python from a previous run, but spare the retrieval server so it
# can be reused across reruns (reloading its ~61GB index takes minutes).
kill_python_except_retriever() {
   local keep pid
   keep=" $(pgrep -f 'local_dense_retriever/retrieval_server.py' 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
   for pid in $(pgrep -f 'python' 2>/dev/null); do
      case "$keep" in
         *" $pid "*) ;;                 # this is the retriever -> keep it
         *) kill -9 "$pid" 2>/dev/null ;;
      esac
   done
}

# for rerun the task
pkill -9 sglang
sleep 3
ray stop --force
pkill -9 ray
kill_python_except_retriever
sleep 3
pkill -9 ray
kill_python_except_retriever

set -ex

# The rollout runs up to search_concurrency (256) concurrent aiohttp requests to
# the local retrieval server, on top of sglang/ray file descriptors. The default
# soft limit (1024) is far too low and the rollout crashes with
# "OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files". Raise it as high as the hard limit
# allows; ray workers launched below inherit this shell's limit.
ulimit -n "$(ulimit -Hn)"

# will prevent ray from buffering stdout/stderr
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

# Online W&B initialization is unreliable from this devspace and a timeout
# kills the RolloutManager actor. Default to local logging; callers can opt in
# with WANDB_MODE=online once network access is stable.
export WANDB_MODE=${WANDB_MODE:-offline}

# The persistent faiss retriever (--faiss_gpu) holds ~9GB more on GPU0 than on the
# other GPUs, so SGLang's TP memory-balance check ("memory capacity is unbalanced")
# fatally aborts the GPU0-paired engine on restart. The imbalance is expected and
# within the mem-fraction-static headroom. NOTE: slime gives each rollout engine an
# isolated ray runtime_env, so exporting the var here does NOT reach those actors --
# the actual disable lives in slime/ray/rollout.py's engine env_vars. This export
# only covers the driver/train side and is kept as defense-in-depth.
export SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK=0

# On the cybertron devspaces an egress whitelist proxy is exported into every
# shell (http_proxy/https_proxy -> whitelist-proxy:7891) with a no_proxy that
# does NOT cover localhost or this node. ray's "ray job submit" then routes its
# request to the local dashboard (127.0.0.1:8265) through that proxy and gets a
# 502 Bad Gateway, and the same happens for sglang's node-local HTTP. Prepend
# the loopback addresses, this node's IP and its /16 to no_proxy so all
# in-cluster / on-node traffic bypasses the proxy. Harmless off-cluster (the
# vars are simply absent). hostname -I is the reliable source for the node IP;
# `ip` is not always on PATH in these non-login shells, so it is only a fallback.
NODE_IP=$(hostname -I 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}') || true
if [ -z "${NODE_IP:-}" ]; then
   NODE_IP=$(ip route get 1.1.1.1 2>/dev/null | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i=="src"){print $(i+1); exit}}') || true
fi
case "${NODE_IP:-}" in
   *.*.*.*)
      PREFIX16=$(echo "$NODE_IP" | awk -F. '{print $1"."$2".0.0/16"}')
      export no_proxy="127.0.0.1,localhost,0.0.0.0,${NODE_IP},${PREFIX16}${no_proxy:+,$no_proxy}"
      export NO_PROXY="$no_proxy" ;;
   *)
      export no_proxy="127.0.0.1,localhost,0.0.0.0${no_proxy:+,$no_proxy}"
      export NO_PROXY="$no_proxy" ;;
esac

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" &>/dev/null && pwd)"
# slime repo root (this recipe lives at <slime>/examples/search-r1)
SLIME_DIR="$(cd -- "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." &>/dev/null && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../scripts/models/qwen2.5-3B.sh"

# Use the HuggingFace mirror for all downloads.
export HF_ENDPOINT=${HF_ENDPOINT:-https://hf-mirror.com}

DATA_DIR=${DATA_DIR:-$PWD}
MODEL_DIR=${MODEL_DIR:-$PWD}
bash "$SCRIPT_DIR/prepare_data.sh"

DATASET_DIR=${DATASET_DIR:-$DATA_DIR/nq_hotpotqa_train}
TRAIN_DATA=${TRAIN_DATA:-$DATASET_DIR/train.parquet}
TEST_DATA=${TEST_DATA:-$DATASET_DIR/test.parquet}

# Model checkpoints under MODEL_DIR: the HF checkpoint and its mcore
# (torch_dist) conversion used as the reference weights.
HF_MODEL_DIR=${HF_MODEL_DIR:-$MODEL_DIR/Qwen2.5-3B}
DIST_MODEL_DIR=${DIST_MODEL_DIR:-$MODEL_DIR/Qwen2.5-3B_torch_dist}

# Download the HF checkpoint if it is not already present under MODEL_DIR.
if [ ! -d "$HF_MODEL_DIR" ] || [ -z "$(ls -A "$HF_MODEL_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
   echo "[model] $HF_MODEL_DIR missing; downloading Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B from $HF_ENDPOINT"
   hf download Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B --local-dir "$HF_MODEL_DIR"
fi

# Convert to a torch_dist (mcore) checkpoint if not already done.
if [ ! -d "$DIST_MODEL_DIR" ] || [ -z "$(ls -A "$DIST_MODEL_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
   echo "[model] converting $HF_MODEL_DIR -> $DIST_MODEL_DIR (torch_dist)"
   PYTHONPATH=${MEGATRON_LM_DIR:-/root/Megatron-LM} python "${SLIME_DIR}/tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py" \
      "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" \
      --hf-checkpoint "$HF_MODEL_DIR" \
      --save "$DIST_MODEL_DIR"
fi

CKPT_ARGS=(
   --hf-checkpoint "$HF_MODEL_DIR"
   --ref-load "$DIST_MODEL_DIR"
   # --load "$MODEL_DIR/Qwen2.5-3B_slime/"
   --save "$MODEL_DIR/Qwen2.5-3B_slime/"
   --save-interval 10
)

# --- the local dense retrieval server ---------------------------------------
# generate_with_search.py posts every search turn to
# http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve, so the rollout cannot start without it.
#
# Started here rather than left to the caller, because none of the three paths
# that run this script are able to start it themselves:
#
#   * the harness's prepare stage is a container created and removed around
#     prepare.sh (evaluation/evaluator.py::_run_prepare, and
#     runtimes/providers/docker.py::close_sandbox is a `docker rm -f`), so a
#     server backgrounded there does not outlive the stage -- and prepare is
#     waited on in the foreground, so starting it there without detaching just
#     hangs until the stage timeout;
#   * on the harbor path prepare can be a build-time RUN layer, which has no
#     GPU at all;
#   * the solution-level instruction forbids the agent from using `&`, nohup,
#     tmux, screen or any other detach mechanism.
#
# A child of this script is none of those things: the script itself still runs
# in the foreground and still owns the exit status. It also has to happen before
# `ray start` below, so that sglang sizes its engines against the memory the
# faiss shards already hold (see the SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK
# note above).
#
# An already-listening server is reused rather than restarted: loading the 60GiB
# index takes minutes, which is the same reason kill_python_except_retriever at
# the top of this file spares it across reruns.
RETRIEVAL_PORT=${RETRIEVAL_PORT:-8000}
RETRIEVAL_LOG=${RETRIEVAL_LOG:-$SLIME_DIR/retrieval_server.log}
# 30 minutes. A *cold* start also has to turn the 14GB corpus into datasets'
# arrow cache, which is the slow half; environment/prepare.sh warms that cache
# so the usual start is a few minutes. The guard has to cover the cold case
# anyway -- nothing guarantees prepare ran.
RETRIEVAL_STARTUP_TIMEOUT=${RETRIEVAL_STARTUP_TIMEOUT:-1800}

# The port opens only after retrieval_server.py has built the retriever (the
# index load and the corpus load both happen before uvicorn.run), so "listening"
# really does mean "ready" -- no separate health request needed.
retrieval_listening() { (exec 3<>"/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/${RETRIEVAL_PORT}") 2>/dev/null; }

# Matches the start script too, not just the server: for the first few seconds
# after launch the process is still the `bash start_retriver.sh` wrapper and has
# not exec'd python yet, and treating that as "already dead" would abort a start
# that is fine.
retrieval_alive() {
   pgrep -f 'local_dense_retriever/retrieval_server.py' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
      || pgrep -f 'search-r1/start_retriver.sh' >/dev/null 2>&1
}

if retrieval_listening; then
   echo "[retrieval] reusing the server already listening on :${RETRIEVAL_PORT}"
else
   echo "[retrieval] starting the local dense retriever (log: $RETRIEVAL_LOG)"
   # Note the spelling: the file is start_retriver.sh, without the second 'e'.
   # It also carries no shebang, so it has to be handed to bash explicitly.
   #
   # DATA_DIR / MODEL_DIR are passed through rather than left to default to
   # $PWD: the server must read the same wiki-18 and e5-base-v2 this run was
   # told about, even when the caller's working directory is not $SLIME_DIR.
   #
   # setsid puts it in its own process group. A *rerun* of this script starts by
   # walking process groups with pkill/ray stop, and keeping the retriever out of
   # this shell's group is what makes kill_python_except_retriever's exemption
   # actually hold.
   #
   # The redirections sit on the *subshell*, not on the setsid command inside it.
   # This is not cosmetic. With `... setsid bash ... >"$LOG" 2>&1 &` the
   # backgrounded AND-list runs in an intermediate subshell that still holds this
   # script's own stdout and stderr, and that subshell outlives the script -- so
   # the retriever, which is meant to survive for the *next* rerun, keeps the
   # write end of this script's stdout pipe open. Whoever is reading that pipe
   # (`| tee .../train.log` under docker/debug-env.sh, the harness's own capture
   # in the agent stage) then never sees EOF, and a finished training run looks
   # like a hung one. Redirecting the subshell leaves no descendant holding it.
   (
      cd "$SLIME_DIR" \
         && DATA_DIR="$DATA_DIR" MODEL_DIR="$MODEL_DIR" \
            setsid bash examples/search-r1/start_retriver.sh &
   ) >"$RETRIEVAL_LOG" 2>&1 </dev/null

   # The wait loop is untraced on purpose: at one probe every 5s a cold start
   # would otherwise put thousands of `set -x` lines into the graded train log.
   # Progress is reported once a minute instead.
   set +x
   retrieval_waited=0
   until retrieval_listening; do
      if ! retrieval_alive; then
         echo "[retrieval] the server exited before it started listening." >&2
         echo "[retrieval] last 40 lines of $RETRIEVAL_LOG:" >&2
         tail -n 40 "$RETRIEVAL_LOG" >&2 || true
         exit 1
      fi
      if [ "$retrieval_waited" -ge "$RETRIEVAL_STARTUP_TIMEOUT" ]; then
         echo "[retrieval] still no listener on :${RETRIEVAL_PORT} after ${RETRIEVAL_STARTUP_TIMEOUT}s." >&2
         echo "[retrieval] last 40 lines of $RETRIEVAL_LOG:" >&2
         tail -n 40 "$RETRIEVAL_LOG" >&2 || true
         exit 1
      fi
      sleep 5
      retrieval_waited=$((retrieval_waited + 5))
      if [ $((retrieval_waited % 60)) -eq 0 ]; then
         echo "[retrieval] loading the index; ${retrieval_waited}s elapsed"
      fi
   done
   set -x
fi
echo "[retrieval] server up on :${RETRIEVAL_PORT}"

def _passages2string(retrieval_result):
    """
    Convert retrieval results to a formatted string.
    This function works with both google_search and local_search results.
    """
    format_reference = ""
    for idx, doc_item in enumerate(retrieval_result):
        content = doc_item["document"]["contents"]
        title = content.split("\n")[0]
        text = "\n".join(content.split("\n")[1:])
        format_reference += f"Doc {idx+1}(Title: {title})\n"

    return format_reference

    """
    Perform search using either local search engine or Google search.
    The search backend is determined by SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["search_backend"].
    """
    backend = SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["search_backend"]

    if backend == "local":
        from local_search_server import local_search

        local_config = SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["local"]
        result = await local_search(
            local_config["search_url"],
            query,
            SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["topk"],
            proxy=local_config["proxy"],
        )
    elif backend == "google":
        from google_search_server import google_search

        google_config = SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["google"]
        result = await google_search(
            google_config["api_key"],
            query,
            SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["topk"],
            snippet_only=google_config["snippet_only"],
            proxy=google_config["proxy"],
        )
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown search backend: {backend}. " f"Must be either 'local' or 'google'.")

    return _passages2string(result)

# on the strings returned from the inference engine (sglang). This is because:
# 1. We don't know how to truncate the corresponding tokens/logp arrays to match the modified string
# 2. Re-tokenizing the postprocessed string may produce different tokens than what the engine generated,
#    leading to misalignment between tokens and their log probabilities
# Therefore, postprocess_responses is only used when return_logprob=False.
def postprocess_responses(resp: str) -> str:
    """
    Post-process response to ensure tag completeness.
    Only used when SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["return_logprob"] is False.
    """
    return (
        resp.split("</search>")[0] + "</search>"
        if "</search>" in resp
        else resp.split("</answer>")[0] + "</answer>" if "</answer>" in resp else resp
    )


def postprocess_predictions(prediction: str):
    pattern = r"<(search|answer)>(.*?)</\1>"
    match = re.search(pattern, prediction, re.DOTALL)
    if match:
        content = match.group(2).strip()  # Return only the content inside the tags
        action = match.group(1)
    else:
        content = ""
        action = None

    return action, content


async def execute_predictions(prediction: str) -> str:
    action, content = postprocess_predictions(prediction)

    if action == "search":
        search_query = content
        async with SEMAPHORE:
            search_results = await search(search_query)
        next_obs = f"\n\n<information>{search_results.strip()}</information>\n\n"
        done = False
    elif action == "answer":
        next_obs = ""
        done = True
    else:
        next_obs = "\nMy previous action is invalid. \
If I want to search, I should put the query between <search> and </search>. \
If I want to give the final answer, I should put the answer between <answer> and </answer>. Let me try again.\n"
        done = False

    return next_obs, done

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Prepare the inputs for the Search-R1 slime recipe:
     3	#   1. the QA dataset  -> nq_hotpotqa_train/{train,test}.parquet
     4	#   2. the retrieval corpus -> wiki-18 e5 FAISS index + wiki-18.jsonl
     5	#
     6	# It drives the data-preparation subset of the Search-R1 repo that ships next to
     7	# this recipe (workspace/Search-R1). Nothing here trains a model.
     8	#
     9	# Usage:
    10	#   bash prepare_data.sh                 # dataset + corpus
    11	#   DATASET_ONLY=1 bash prepare_data.sh  # skip the ~130GB corpus download
    12	#   CORPUS_ONLY=1  bash prepare_data.sh  # only the retrieval corpus
    13	#
    14	# Override any path via the environment variables below.
    15	set -euo pipefail
    16	
    17	# --- locations -------------------------------------------------------------
    18	# Directory of this script (examples/search-r1), resolved so it works from any cwd.
    19	HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    20	
    21	# The trimmed Search-R1 repo. Defaults to the copy staged in this workspace
    22	# (workspace/Search-R1); at container runtime the recipe reads /root/Search-R1,
    23	# so allow an override.
    24	SEARCH_R1_DIR="${SEARCH_R1_DIR:-$(cd "$HERE/../../Search-R1" && pwd)}"
    25	
    26	# Where prepared assets land. Keep them inside the repo's data/ dir so the paths
    27	# match the recipe's --prompt-data (…/Search-R1/data/nq_hotpotqa_train/…).
    28	DATA_DIR="${DATA_DIR:-$PWD}"
    29	DATASET_DIR="${DATASET_DIR:-$DATA_DIR/nq_hotpotqa_train}"
    30	CORPUS_DIR="${CORPUS_DIR:-$DATA_DIR/wiki-18}"
    31	
    32	# Which QA sources to merge. Train mixes NQ+HotpotQA (the recipe default); the
    33	# test merge can span more sets for evaluation.
    34	TRAIN_SOURCES="${TRAIN_SOURCES:-nq,hotpotqa}"
    35	TEST_SOURCES="${TEST_SOURCES:-nq,hotpotqa}"
    36	
    37	DATASET_ONLY="${DATASET_ONLY:-0}"
    38	CORPUS_ONLY="${CORPUS_ONLY:-0}"
    39	# Re-download even if the target files already exist.
    40	FORCE="${FORCE:-0}"
    41	
    42	if [[ ! -d "$SEARCH_R1_DIR/scripts/data_process" ]]; then
    43	  echo "error: Search-R1 data-prep scripts not found under: $SEARCH_R1_DIR" >&2
    44	  echo "       set SEARCH_R1_DIR to the trimmed Search-R1 repo." >&2
    45	  exit 1
    46	fi
    47	
    48	# The merge scripts import verl.utils.hdfs_io from the repo root.
    49	export PYTHONPATH="$SEARCH_R1_DIR${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
    50	
    51	# --- 1) QA dataset ---------------------------------------------------------
    52	prepare_dataset() {
    53	  local train_parquet="$DATASET_DIR/train.parquet"
    54	  local test_parquet="$DATASET_DIR/test.parquet"
    55	
    56	  if [[ "$FORCE" != "1" && -f "$train_parquet" && -f "$test_parquet" ]]; then
    57	    echo "==> QA parquet already present, skipping ($DATASET_DIR)"
    58	    echo "    -> $train_parquet"
    59	    echo "    -> $test_parquet"
    60	    return
    61	  fi
    62	
    63	  echo "==> Building QA parquet into $DATASET_DIR"
    64	  echo "    train sources: $TRAIN_SOURCES"
    65	  echo "    test  sources: $TEST_SOURCES"
    66	  mkdir -p "$DATASET_DIR"
    67	
    68	  if [[ "$FORCE" != "1" && -f "$train_parquet" ]]; then
    69	    echo "    train.parquet exists, skipping train merge"
    70	  else
    71	    python "$SEARCH_R1_DIR/scripts/data_process/qa_search_train_merge.py" \
    72	      --local_dir "$DATASET_DIR" --data_sources "$TRAIN_SOURCES"
    73	  fi
    74	
    75	  if [[ "$FORCE" != "1" && -f "$test_parquet" ]]; then
    76	    echo "    test.parquet exists, skipping test merge"
    77	  else
    78	    python "$SEARCH_R1_DIR/scripts/data_process/qa_search_test_merge.py" \
    79	      --local_dir "$DATASET_DIR" --data_sources "$TEST_SOURCES"
    80	  fi
    81	
    82	  echo "    -> $train_parquet"
    83	  echo "    -> $test_parquet"
    84	}
    85	
    86	# --- 2) retrieval corpus (wiki-18 e5) --------------------------------------
    87	prepare_corpus() {

    89	  local jsonl="$CORPUS_DIR/wiki-18.jsonl"

    92	    echo "==> wiki-18 corpus already present, skipping ($CORPUS_DIR)"
    93	    echo "    -> $index"

    98	  echo "==> Downloading wiki-18 e5 index + corpus into $CORPUS_DIR"
    99	  echo "    NOTE: the assembled index is ~130GB; ensure disk + bandwidth."
   100	  mkdir -p "$CORPUS_DIR"
   101	
   102	  # Pulls PeterJinGo/wiki-18-e5-index (part_aa, part_ab) and
   103	  # PeterJinGo/wiki-18-corpus (wiki-18.jsonl.gz) from the HuggingFace Hub.
   104	  python "$SEARCH_R1_DIR/scripts/download.py" --save_path "$CORPUS_DIR"

   107	  cat "$CORPUS_DIR"/part_* > "$index"

   110	  if [[ -f "$CORPUS_DIR/wiki-18.jsonl.gz" ]]; then
   111	    echo "    Decompressing wiki-18.jsonl"
   112	    gzip -df "$CORPUS_DIR/wiki-18.jsonl.gz"
   113	  fi
   114	
   115	  echo "    -> $index"
   116	  echo "    -> $jsonl"
   117	}

   121	  prepare_corpus
   122	elif [[ "$DATASET_ONLY" == "1" ]]; then
   123	  prepare_dataset
   124	else

   127	fi

===== local_search =====
     1	"""
     2	Local Search Server for Search-R1
     3	
     4	This module provides a local search engine interface that mimics the google_search_server.py API.
     5	It sends requests to a local retrieval server (e.g., running retrieval_server.py from Search-R1)
     6	and formats the results to match the expected output format.
     7	
     8	Usage:
     9	    In your generate_with_search.py, replace:
    10	        from google_search_server import google_search
    11	    with:
    12	        from local_search_server import local_search as google_search
    13	
    14	    And update SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS:
    15	        SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS = {
    16	            "search_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve",  # URL of local retrieval server
    17	            "topk": 3,
    18	            ...
    19	        }
    20	"""
    21	
    22	import aiohttp
    23	
    24	
    25	async def local_search(
    26	    search_url: str,
    27	    query: str,
    28	    top_k: int = 5,
    29	    timeout: int = 60,
    30	    proxy: str | None = None,
    31	) -> list[dict]:
    32	    """
    33	    Call local search engine server and format results to match google_search_server.py output.
    34	
    35	    This function provides the same interface as google_search() from google_search_server.py,
    36	    making it a drop-in replacement. The only difference is that instead of using an API key,
    37	    it uses a search_url parameter.
    38	
    39	    Args:
    40	        search_url: URL of the local retrieval server (e.g., "http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve")
    41	        query: Search query string
    42	        top_k: Number of results to retrieve
    43	        timeout: Request timeout in seconds (default: 60)
    44	        proxy: Proxy URL if needed (not used for local retrieval, kept for API compatibility)
    45	        snippet_only: If True, only return snippet (kept for API compatibility with google_search)
    46	
    47	    Returns:
    48	        List of dictionaries with format: [{"document": {"contents": '"<title>"\n<text>'}}]
    49	        This matches the output format of google_search() from google_search_server.py
    50	    """
    51	    # Prepare request payload for local retrieval server
    52	    payload = {
    53	        "queries": [query],
    54	        "topk": top_k,
    55	        "return_scores": False,  # We don't need scores for compatibility with google_search_server
    56	    }
    57	
    58	    # Send async request to local retrieval server
    59	    timeout_obj = aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=timeout)
    60	    session_kwargs = {}
    61	    # Note: proxy parameter is kept for API compatibility but typically not needed for local server
    62	    if proxy:
    63	        session_kwargs["proxy"] = proxy
    64	
    65	    try:
    66	        async with aiohttp.ClientSession(**session_kwargs) as session:
    67	            async with session.post(search_url, json=payload, timeout=timeout_obj) as resp:

def _prefix_config_keys(config, prefix):
    return {f"{prefix}/{key}": value for key, value in config.items()}


def _get_role_args_for_logging(args, role):
    if getattr(args, "megatron_config_path", None) is None:
        return args

    from slime.utils.arguments import parse_megatron_role_args

    return parse_megatron_role_args(args, args.megatron_config_path, role=role)


def _compute_secondary_config_for_logging(args, role=None):
    config = _args_to_config_dict(args)
    if role == "critic":
        return _prefix_config_keys(config, "critic")
    return config


# https://docs.wandb.ai/guides/track/log/distributed-training/#track-all-processes-to-a-single-run
def init_wandb_secondary(args, role=None):
    wandb_run_id = getattr(args, "wandb_run_id", None)
    if wandb_run_id is None:
        return

    # Set W&B mode if specified (same as primary)
    if args.wandb_mode:
        os.environ["WANDB_MODE"] = args.wandb_mode

    offline = _is_offline_mode(args)

    if (not offline) and args.wandb_key is not None:
        wandb.login(key=args.wandb_key, host=args.wandb_host)

    # Configure settings based on offline/online mode
    if offline:
        settings_kwargs = dict(mode="offline")
    else:
        settings_kwargs = dict(
            mode="shared",
            x_primary=False,
            x_update_finish_state=False,
        )

    init_kwargs = {
        "id": wandb_run_id,
        "entity": args.wandb_team,
        "project": args.wandb_project,
        "config": _compute_secondary_config_for_logging(args, role=role),
        "resume": "allow",
        "reinit": True,
        "settings": wandb.Settings(**settings_kwargs),
    }

    # Add custom directory if specified
    if args.wandb_dir:
        os.makedirs(args.wandb_dir, exist_ok=True)
        init_kwargs["dir"] = args.wandb_dir

    wandb.init(**init_kwargs)

    _init_wandb_common()


def _init_wandb_common():
    wandb.define_metric("train/step")
    wandb.define_metric("train/*", step_metric="train/step")
    wandb.define_metric("rollout/step")
    wandb.define_metric("rollout/*", step_metric="rollout/step")
    wandb.define_metric("multi_turn/*", step_metric="rollout/step")
    wandb.define_metric("passrate/*", step_metric="rollout/step")
    wandb.define_metric("eval/step")
    wandb.define_metric("eval/*", step_metric="eval/step")
    wandb.define_metric("perf/*", step_metric="rollout/step")

To implement multi-turn conversation + tool-calling in slime, you only need to implement a custom data generation function and a reward model for the task. These correspond to the following 2 configuration items in the startup script:

## Appendix: Setting up Local Retriever

This section provides detailed instructions for setting up the local dense retriever for use with the local search backend.

### Prerequisites

The local retriever requires a separate conda environment to avoid conflicts with the training environment. It uses GPU for efficient retrieval.

### Step 1: Install Conda

If you don't have conda installed, run the following commands:

corpus_file=$save_path/wiki-18.jsonl

**Important Notes:**

### Step 5: Start Training

steps.message: I found two implementation defects that explain the training/evaluation pattern. The search formatter computes each passage’s body but emits only its title, so search returns almost no evidence; and the custom rollout builds a correct non-trainable mask for tool observations, then overwrites it with an all-ones mask before returning. The reward call also supplies `format_score` under a parameter the staged scorer does not use, leaving its intended partial format/retrieval rewards at zero. I’m repairing those paths while preserving the protected scorer, datasets, retriever, and required eval wiring.

import os
import shutil

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
from megatron.core.enums import ModelType
from megatron.training.arguments import parse_args, validate_args
from megatron.training.checkpointing import get_checkpoint_name, get_checkpoint_tracker_filename, save_checkpoint
from megatron.training.training import get_model

from slime.backends.megatron_utils.arguments import set_default_megatron_args
from slime.backends.megatron_utils.hf_to_megatron import load_hf_weights
from slime.backends.megatron_utils.initialize import init
from slime.backends.megatron_utils.model_provider import get_model_provider_func
from slime.utils.logging_utils import configure_logger
from slime.utils.memory_utils import print_memory


def add_convertion_args(parser):
    """Add conversion arguments to the parser"""
    parser.add_argument("--hf-checkpoint", type=str, required=True, help="HuggingFace model path")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--custom-model-provider-path",
        type=str,
        default=None,
        help="Path to a custom model provider function.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--allgather-cp", action="store_true", default=False)
    try:
        parser.add_argument("--use-gated-attention", action="store_true", default=False)
    except Exception:
        pass
    try:
        parser.add_argument("--padded-vocab-size", type=int, default=None)
    except Exception:
        pass
    return parser


def get_args():
    args = parse_args(add_convertion_args)
    args = set_default_megatron_args(args)

    # set to pass megatron validate_args
    args.save_interval = 1
    args.micro_batch_size = 1
    world_size = int(os.environ.get("WORLD_SIZE", "1"))
    args.global_batch_size = int(os.environ.get("WORLD_SIZE", "1"))

    assert world_size <= args.num_layers, (
        f"World size {world_size} must be less than or equal to number of layers {args.num_layers}. "
        "You are using too many GPUs for this conversion."
    )

    def ceildiv(a, b):
        return -(a // -b)

    if args.pipeline_model_parallel_size == 1 and world_size > 1:
        pp_size = world_size
        while True:
            args.pipeline_model_parallel_size = pp_size
            args.decoder_last_pipeline_num_layers = args.num_layers - ceildiv(
                args.num_layers, args.pipeline_model_parallel_size
            ) * (args.pipeline_model_parallel_size - 1)

            if args.decoder_last_pipeline_num_layers > 0:
                break

            if pp_size % 2 == 0:
                pp_size //= 2
            else:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Cannot find a valid pipeline model parallel size for {args.num_layers} layers and {world_size} GPUs."
                )
    print(
        f"Using pipeline model parallel size: {args.pipeline_model_parallel_size}, decoder last pipeline num layers: {args.decoder_last_pipeline_num_layers}"
    )

    validate_args(args)
    return args


def main():
    if torch.version.hip:
        import megatron.core.dist_checkpointing.strategies.filesystem_async as filesystem_async_module
        from slime.utils.rocm_checkpoint_writer import ROCmFileSystemWriterAsync

        filesystem_async_module.FileSystemWriterAsync = ROCmFileSystemWriterAsync
        print("[ROCm] Applied FileSystemWriterAsync patch for HIP compatibility")

    configure_logger()

    # Initialize distributed environment
    world_size = int(os.getenv("WORLD_SIZE") or os.getenv("SLURM_NTASKS") or 1)
    local_rank = int(os.getenv("LOCAL_RANK") or os.getenv("SLURM_LOCALID") or 0)
    global_rank = int(os.getenv("RANK") or os.getenv("SLURM_PROCID") or 0)

    torch.cuda.set_device(local_rank)
    os.environ.setdefault("WORLD_SIZE", str(world_size))
    os.environ.setdefault("RANK", str(global_rank))
    os.environ.setdefault("LOCAL_RANK", str(local_rank))
    os.environ.setdefault("MASTER_ADDR", "localhost")
    os.environ.setdefault("MASTER_PORT", "12355")
    dist.init_process_group(
        backend="nccl",
        world_size=world_size,
        rank=global_rank,
        device_id=torch.device(f"cuda:{local_rank}"),
    )
    args = get_args()
    init(args)

    # if using AMD gpus, we have to do the conversion in cpu
    if hasattr(torch.version, "hip") and torch.version.hip is not None:
        assert args.use_cpu_initialization, "AMD GPU requires --use_cpu_initialization=True"

    model = get_model(get_model_provider_func(args), ModelType.encoder_or_decoder, wrap_with_ddp=False)

    # Load model
    hf_model_path = args.hf_checkpoint
    load_hf_weights(args, model, hf_model_path)
    print(f"Model loaded: {hf_model_path}")

    if args.use_cpu_initialization:
        model[0] = model[0].cpu()

    print_memory("after loading model")
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    gc.collect()
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()

    save_checkpoint(1, model, None, None, 0)

    if dist.get_rank() == 0:
        # change to release ckpt
        tracker_filename = get_checkpoint_tracker_filename(args.save)
        with open(tracker_filename, "w") as f:
            f.write("release")
        source_dir = get_checkpoint_name(args.save, 1, False, return_base_dir=True)
        target_dir = get_checkpoint_name(args.save, -1, True, return_base_dir=True)
        shutil.move(source_dir, target_dir)
    dist.barrier()
    dist.destroy_process_group()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

+# Ray's driver and actors otherwise default to ./wandb inside their isolated

from enum import Enum
from typing import Any

import torch

from slime.utils.misc import decode_int32_meta_array

_TOP_P_TOKEN_ID_META_KEYS = ("top_p_token_ids", "top_p_kept_token_ids")
_TOP_P_TOKEN_OFFSET_META_KEYS = ("top_p_token_offsets", "top_p_kept_token_offsets")


def _extract_rollout_top_p_token_data(
    meta_info: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    expected_num_tokens: int | None = None,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor] | None:
    token_ids = decode_int32_meta_array(meta_info, _TOP_P_TOKEN_ID_META_KEYS)
    offsets = decode_int32_meta_array(meta_info, _TOP_P_TOKEN_OFFSET_META_KEYS)
    if token_ids is None and offsets is None:
        return None
    if token_ids is None or offsets is None:
        raise ValueError("SGLang top-p token replay must include both token ids and offsets.")
    if offsets.numel() == 0 or int(offsets[0]) != 0:
        raise ValueError(f"SGLang top-p token offsets must start with 0, got {offsets[:1].tolist()}.")
    if int(offsets[-1]) != token_ids.numel():
        raise ValueError(
            "SGLang top-p token ids/offsets mismatch: "
            f"offsets[-1]={int(offsets[-1])}, len(token_ids)={token_ids.numel()}."
        )
    if expected_num_tokens is not None and offsets.numel() != expected_num_tokens + 1:
        raise ValueError(
            "SGLang top-p token offsets length must equal generated token count + 1: "
            f"len(offsets)={offsets.numel()}, generated={expected_num_tokens}."
        )
    return token_ids, offsets


def _merge_rollout_top_p_token_data(
    base_token_ids: list[int] | torch.Tensor | None,
    base_offsets: list[int] | torch.Tensor | None,
    token_ids: torch.Tensor,
    offsets: torch.Tensor,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    base_token_ids = torch.as_tensor([] if base_token_ids is None else base_token_ids, dtype=torch.int32).reshape(-1)
    base_offsets = torch.as_tensor([0] if base_offsets is None else base_offsets, dtype=torch.int32).reshape(-1)
    base_offset = int(base_offsets[-1])
    return (
        torch.cat([base_token_ids, token_ids]),
        torch.cat([base_offsets, offsets[1:] + base_offset]),
    )


def _pad_rollout_top_p_offsets(
    token_ids: list[int] | torch.Tensor | None,
    offsets: list[int] | torch.Tensor | None,
    num_tokens: int,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    if offsets is None or token_ids is None:
        raise ValueError("Cannot append empty top-p spans without existing token ids and offsets.")
    if num_tokens < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"num_tokens must be non-negative, got {num_tokens}.")
    token_ids = torch.as_tensor(token_ids, dtype=torch.int32).reshape(-1)
    offsets = torch.as_tensor(offsets, dtype=torch.int32).reshape(-1)
    if offsets.numel() == 0:
        raise ValueError("Cannot append empty top-p spans to empty offsets.")
    if num_tokens == 0:
        return token_ids, offsets
    empty_offsets = offsets.new_full((num_tokens,), int(offsets[-1]))
    return token_ids, torch.cat([offsets, empty_offsets])


def _to_int_list(tokens) -> list[int]:
    if tokens is None:
        return []
    if torch.is_tensor(tokens):
        return [int(token) for token in tokens.detach().cpu().reshape(-1).tolist()]
    return [int(token) for token in tokens]


def _to_float_list(values) -> list[float] | None:
    if values is None:
        return None
    if torch.is_tensor(values):
        return [float(value) for value in values.detach().cpu().reshape(-1).tolist()]
    return [float(value) for value in values]


def _numel(value) -> int:
    return int(torch.as_tensor(value).reshape(-1).numel())


@dataclass
class Sample:
    """The sample generated"""

    group_index: int | None = None
    index: int | None = None

const report = `# Staged experiment diagnosis

## Verdict

**Unhealthy.** The frozen held-out metric is the deciding evidence: \`eval/nq_test\` rises from 0.033 at step 0 to only 0.1673 at step 199, then plateaus and fluctuates. At the same time, the rollout behavior collapses from a mean response length of 1,038 tokens with 0.3828 truncation to about 9 tokens with zero truncation. Held-out responses show the same collapse (932.8 tokens / 0.3637 truncation at the first eval versus 12.2 tokens / 0.00067 truncation at the last). The historical runtime also falls from roughly 29 seconds per rollout to about 2 seconds. This is a short-output degeneracy, not healthy post-training search behavior.

The rising training \`raw_reward\` (about 0.035 initially and up to roughly 0.36 later) does not establish health: the logged normalized rollout rewards and advantages are essentially zero, and many groups have zero reward variance. The held-out score and rollout signals therefore outweigh the training reward trend.

## Root cause

Three defects connected the implementation to the observed behavior:

1. In [generate_with_search.py](/workspace/examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py:44), \`_passages2string\` extracted each retrieved document's body into \`text\` but emitted only the title. Search observations consequently contained almost no evidence. That prevents the model from using the local retriever on the QA task and explains why the run can become fast and short without reaching strong held-out exact match.

2. The custom rollout appended retrieval observations as non-trainable through \`sample.append_response_tokens(..., trainable=False)\`, but separately added those observation tokens to its local \`loss_mask\` with ones and overwrote \`sample.loss_mask\` with that mask at the end. Tool/context tokens were therefore optimized as if they were policy output. The historical response-length/truncation collapse is consistent with this corrupted training signal. Observation positions now receive zero loss-mask entries.

3. The reward call passed \`format_score=0.2\` to [qa_em_format.py](/workspace/examples/search-r1/qa_em_format.py:156), but that staged, read-only scorer does not use its legacy \`format_score\` parameter. Its partial-credit branches use \`structure_format_score\`, \`final_format_score\`, and \`retrieval_score\`, all of which therefore stayed at zero. The policy received a sparse exact-match signal while invalid/partial trajectories received no useful shaping. The call now supplies the intended 0.2 structure credit and 0.1 retrieval/final-format credits.

## Changes

- [generate_with_search.py](/workspace/examples/search-r1/generate_with_search.py:44)
  - Include retrieved passage bodies in the information observation.
  - Mask retrieval observation tokens as non-trainable.
  - Pass the scorer's actual partial-credit parameters to the custom reward function.
- [run_qwen2.5_3B.sh](/workspace/examples/search-r1/run_qwen2.5_3B.sh:38)
  - Pin model, reference checkpoint, datasets, corpus, and working directory to the staged \`/workspace\` assets.
  - Remove the network-dependent data/model download path.
  - Set \`--num-rollout 100\), retaining the required eval interval, \`nq_test\` \`[0:3000]\` slice, one eval sample, and custom generate/reward paths.
  - Route Ray/W&B artifacts and the foreground job log under \`$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs\` (W&B under its \`wandb\` subdirectory).
  - Make the offline W&B mode/key handling explicit and tolerate the placeholder key.
  - Keep the local retriever endpoint at \`http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve\`.

Protected scorer, retriever, and dataset files were not modified.

## Expected effect

The main success metric should be \`eval/nq_test\`, moving upward from the frozen ~0.167 plateau. The raw reward/pass rate should become more informative, with fewer zero-variance groups and nontrivial normalized advantages. Search rollouts should retain useful generated reasoning and evidence use instead of converging to the observed 9–12-token behavior; the response-length metric will now count policy-generated tokens rather than retrieval context tokens. The launch changes ensure the rerun uses the required 100-rollout budget and leaves gradeable train/W&B metrics in the required directory.
`;
const r = await tools.exec_command({cmd:`cat > report.md <<'EOF'\n${report}\nEOF\nwc -c report.md && sed -n '1,260p' report.md`,workdir:"/workspace",yield_time_ms:10000,max_output_tokens:30000});

#!/bin/bash

# Kill leftover python from a previous run, but spare the retrieval server so it
# can be reused across reruns (reloading its ~61GB index takes minutes).
kill_python_except_retriever() {
   local keep pid
   keep=" $(pgrep -f 'local_dense_retriever/retrieval_server.py' 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
   for pid in $(pgrep -f 'python' 2>/dev/null); do
      case "$keep" in
         *" $pid "*) ;;                 # this is the retriever -> keep it
         *) kill -9 "$pid" 2>/dev/null ;;
      esac
   done
}

mkdir -p "$RESULT_LOG_DIR/wandb"
TRAIN_LOG="$RESULT_LOG_DIR/train.log"

# other GPUs, so SGLang's TP memory-balance check ("memory capacity is unbalanced")
# fatally aborts the GPU0-paired engine on restart. The imbalance is expected and
# within the mem-fraction-static headroom. NOTE: slime gives each rollout engine an
# isolated ray runtime_env, so exporting the var here does NOT reach those actors --
# the actual disable lives in slime/ray/rollout.py's engine env_vars. This export
# only covers the driver/train side and is kept as defense-in-depth.
export SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK=0

# shell (http_proxy/https_proxy -> whitelist-proxy:7891) with a no_proxy that
# does NOT cover localhost or this node. ray's "ray job submit" then routes its
# request to the local dashboard (127.0.0.1:8265) through that proxy and gets a
# 502 Bad Gateway, and the same happens for sglang's node-local HTTP. Prepend
# the loopback addresses, this node's IP and its /16 to no_proxy so all
# in-cluster / on-node traffic bypasses the proxy. Harmless off-cluster (the
# vars are simply absent). hostname -I is the reliable source for the node IP;
# `ip` is not always on PATH in these non-login shells, so it is only a fallback.
NODE_IP=$(hostname -I 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}') || true
if [ -z "${NODE_IP:-}" ]; then
   NODE_IP=$(ip route get 1.1.1.1 2>/dev/null | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i=="src"){print $(i+1); exit}}') || true
fi
case "${NODE_IP:-}" in
   *.*.*.*)
      PREFIX16=$(echo "$NODE_IP" | awk -F. '{print $1"."$2".0.0/16"}')
      export no_proxy="127.0.0.1,localhost,0.0.0.0,${NODE_IP},${PREFIX16}${no_proxy:+,$no_proxy}"

# --- the local dense retrieval server ---------------------------------------
# generate_with_search.py posts every search turn to
# http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve, so the rollout cannot start without it.
#
# Started here rather than left to the caller, because none of the three paths
# that run this script are able to start it themselves:
#
#   * the harness's prepare stage is a container created and removed around
#     prepare.sh (evaluation/evaluator.py::_run_prepare, and
#     runtimes/providers/docker.py::close_sandbox is a `docker rm -f`), so a
#     server backgrounded there does not outlive the stage -- and prepare is
#     waited on in the foreground, so starting it there without detaching just
#     hangs until the stage timeout;
#   * on the harbor path prepare can be a build-time RUN layer, which has no
#     GPU at all;
#   * the solution-level instruction forbids the agent from using `&`, nohup,
#     tmux, screen or any other detach mechanism.
#
# A child of this script is none of those things: the script itself still runs
# in the foreground and still owns the exit status. It also has to happen before
# `ray start` below, so that sglang sizes its engines against the memory the
# faiss shards already hold (see the SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK

#
# An already-listening server is reused rather than restarted: loading the 60GiB
# index takes minutes, which is the same reason kill_python_except_retriever at

RETRIEVAL_PORT=${RETRIEVAL_PORT:-8000}
RETRIEVAL_LOG=${RETRIEVAL_LOG:-$SLIME_DIR/retrieval_server.log}

# arrow cache, which is the slow half; environment/prepare.sh warms that cache
# so the usual start is a few minutes. The guard has to cover the cold case

RETRIEVAL_STARTUP_TIMEOUT=${RETRIEVAL_STARTUP_TIMEOUT:-1800}

retrieval_listening() { (exec 3<>"/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/${RETRIEVAL_PORT}") 2>/dev/null; }

# after launch the process is still the `bash start_retriver.sh` wrapper and has
# not exec'd python yet, and treating that as "already dead" would abort a start
# that is fine.
retrieval_alive() {

      || pgrep -f 'search-r1/start_retriver.sh' >/dev/null 2>&1
}

if retrieval_listening; then
   echo "[retrieval] reusing the server already listening on :${RETRIEVAL_PORT}"
else
   echo "[retrieval] starting the local dense retriever (log: $RETRIEVAL_LOG)"
   # Note the spelling: the file is start_retriver.sh, without the second 'e'.
   # It also carries no shebang, so it has to be handed to bash explicitly.
   #
   # DATA_DIR / MODEL_DIR are passed through rather than left to default to
   # $PWD: the server must read the same wiki-18 and e5-base-v2 this run was

   # walking process groups with pkill/ray stop, and keeping the retriever out of
   # this shell's group is what makes kill_python_except_retriever's exemption
   # actually hold.
   #
   # The redirections sit on the *subshell*, not on the setsid command inside it.
   # This is not cosmetic. With `... setsid bash ... >"$LOG" 2>&1 &` the
   # backgrounded AND-list runs in an intermediate subshell that still holds this
   # script's own stdout and stderr, and that subshell outlives the script -- so
   # the retriever, which is meant to survive for the *next* rerun, keeps the
   # write end of this script's stdout pipe open. Whoever is reading that pipe
   # (`| tee .../train.log` under docker/debug-env.sh, the harness's own capture
   # in the agent stage) then never sees EOF, and a finished training run looks
   # like a hung one. Redirecting the subshell leaves no descendant holding it.
   (
      cd "$SLIME_DIR" \
         && DATA_DIR="$DATA_DIR" MODEL_DIR="$MODEL_DIR" \
            setsid bash examples/search-r1/start_retriver.sh &
   ) >"$RETRIEVAL_LOG" 2>&1 </dev/null

   # would otherwise put thousands of `set -x` lines into the graded train log.
   # Progress is reported once a minute instead.
   set +x
   retrieval_waited=0
   until retrieval_listening; do

         echo "[retrieval] the server exited before it started listening." >&2
         echo "[retrieval] last 40 lines of $RETRIEVAL_LOG:" >&2
         tail -n 40 "$RETRIEVAL_LOG" >&2 || true
         exit 1
      fi
      if [ "$retrieval_waited" -ge "$RETRIEVAL_STARTUP_TIMEOUT" ]; then
         echo "[retrieval] still no listener on :${RETRIEVAL_PORT} after ${RETRIEVAL_STARTUP_TIMEOUT}s." >&2
         echo "[retrieval] last 40 lines of $RETRIEVAL_LOG:" >&2
         tail -n 40 "$RETRIEVAL_LOG" >&2 || true
         exit 1
      fi
      sleep 5
      retrieval_waited=$((retrieval_waited + 5))
      if [ $((retrieval_waited % 60)) -eq 0 ]; then
         echo "[retrieval] loading the index; ${retrieval_waited}s elapsed"
      fi

# Adapted from https://github.com/PeterGriffinJin/Search-R1/blob/ceee7b89655ed52f205b9beb98e1190c3eedcfb0/search_r1/llm_agent/generation.py
# This is a unified version supporting both local search and Google search, with optional log probability collection

import asyncio
import re

from qa_em_format import compute_score_em

from slime.rollout.sglang_rollout import GenerateState
from slime.utils.http_utils import post
from slime.utils.types import Sample

# Configuration for Search-R1
SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS = {
    # ============== General Configuration ==============
    "max_turns": 8,
    "topk": 3,
    "search_concurrency": 256,
    # ============== Search Backend Selection ==============
    "search_backend": "local",  # Options: "local" or "google"
    # ============== Local Search Configuration ==============
    # (Only used when search_backend="local")
    "local": {
        "search_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve",  # URL of your local retrieval server
        "proxy": None,  # Set to your proxy if needed
    },
    # ============== Google Search Configuration ==============
    # (Only used when search_backend="google")
    "google": {
        "api_key": "your_api_key_here",  # Replace with your actual API key
        "snippet_only": True,  # Set to True to only return snippets
        "proxy": None,  # Set to your proxy if needed
    },
    # ============== Log Probability Collection ==============
    "return_logprob": True,  # Set to True to collect log probabilities for TIS metrics
    # ============== Reward Model Configuration ==============
    "format_score": 0.2,
}


SEMAPHORE = asyncio.Semaphore(SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["search_concurrency"])


def _passages2string(retrieval_result):
    """
    Convert retrieval results to a formatted string.
    This function works with both google_search and local_search results.
    """
    format_reference = ""
    for idx, doc_item in enumerate(retrieval_result):
        content = doc_item["document"]["contents"]
        title = content.split("\n")[0]
        text = "\n".join(content.split("\n")[1:])
        # Keep the passage body in the observation.  The previous formatter
        # computed ``text`` and then dropped it, so search returned titles only
        # and the model had no retrieved evidence to reason over.
        format_reference += f"Doc {idx+1}(Title: {title}) {text}\n"

    return format_reference


async def search(query: str) -> str:
    """
    Perform search using either local search engine or Google search.
    The search backend is determined by SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["search_backend"].
    """
    backend = SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["search_backend"]

    if backend == "local":
        from local_search_server import local_search

        local_config = SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["local"]
        result = await local_search(
            local_config["search_url"],
            query,
            SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["topk"],
            proxy=local_config["proxy"],
        )
    elif backend == "google":
        from google_search_server import google_search

        google_config = SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["google"]
        result = await google_search(
            google_config["api_key"],
            query,
            SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["topk"],
            snippet_only=google_config["snippet_only"],
            proxy=google_config["proxy"],
        )
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown search backend: {backend}. " f"Must be either 'local' or 'google'.")

    return _passages2string(result)


# IMPORTANT: When we need to collect log probabilities (logp), we CANNOT do any postprocessing
# on the strings returned from the inference engine (sglang). This is because:
# 1. We don't know how to truncate the corresponding tokens/logp arrays to match the modified string
# 2. Re-tokenizing the postprocessed string may produce different tokens than what the engine generated,
#    leading to misalignment between tokens and their log probabilities
# Therefore, postprocess_responses is only used when return_logprob=False.
def postprocess_responses(resp: str) -> str:
    """
    Post-process response to ensure tag completeness.
    Only used when SEARCH_R1_CONFIGS["return_logprob"] is False.
    """
    return (
        resp.split("</search>")[0] + "</search>"
        if "</search>" in resp
        else resp.split("</answer>")[0] + "</answer>" if "</answer>" in resp else resp
    )


def postprocess_predictions(prediction: str):
    pattern = r"<(search|answer)>(.*?)</\1>"
    match = re.search(pattern, prediction, re.DOTALL)
    if match:
        content = match.group(2).strip()  # Return only the content inside the tags
        action = match.group(1)
    else:
        content = ""
        action = None

    return action, content


async def execute_predictions(prediction: str) -> str:
    action, content = postprocess_predictions(prediction)

    if action == "search":
        search_query = content
        async with SEMAPHORE:
            search_results = await search(search_query)
        next_obs = f"\n\n<information>{search_results.strip()}</information>\n\n"
        done = False
    elif action == "answer":
        next_obs = ""
        done = True
    else:
        next_obs = "\nMy previous action is invalid. \
If I want to search, I should put the query between <search> and </search>. \
If I want to give the final answer, I should put the answer between <answer> and </answer>. Let me try again.\n"
        done = False

    return next_obs, done


async def generate(args, sample: Sample, sampling_params) -> Sample:
    assert not args.partial_rollout, "Partial rollout is not supported for this function at the moment."

    state = GenerateState(args)

    url = f"http://{args.sglang_router_ip}:{args.sglang_router_port}/generate"

    # Handle partial rollout samples: continue generation from existing response
    prompt_text = sample.prompt
    prompt_tokens_ids = state.tokenizer(prompt_text, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
    sample.tokens = list(prompt_tokens_ids)
    sample.loss_mask = []
    response = ""

     3	# Kill leftover python from a previous run, but spare the retrieval server so it
     4	# can be reused across reruns (reloading its ~61GB index takes minutes).
     5	kill_python_except_retriever() {

     8	   for pid in $(pgrep -f 'python' 2>/dev/null); do
     9	      case "$keep" in
    10	         *" $pid "*) ;;                 # this is the retriever -> keep it
    11	         *) kill -9 "$pid" 2>/dev/null ;;
    12	      esac
    13	   done
    14	}
    15	
    16	# for rerun the task
    17	pkill -9 sglang
    18	sleep 3
    19	ray stop --force

    21	kill_python_except_retriever
    22	sleep 3
    23	pkill -9 ray

    26	set -ex
    27	
    28	# The rollout runs up to search_concurrency (256) concurrent aiohttp requests to
    29	# the local retrieval server, on top of sglang/ray file descriptors. The default
    30	# soft limit (1024) is far too low and the rollout crashes with
    31	# "OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files". Raise it as high as the hard limit
    32	# allows; ray workers launched below inherit this shell's limit.
    33	ulimit -n "$(ulimit -Hn)"
    34	
    35	# will prevent ray from buffering stdout/stderr
    36	export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
    37	
    38	# All fresh-run artifacts are graded from this directory.  The harness provides
    39	# AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS; use a local fallback for manual/static invocation.
    40	RESULT_LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-${AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS:-/workspace}/experiment_logs}"

    43	export RESULT_LOG_DIR TRAIN_LOG

    45	# Online W&B initialization is unreliable from this devspace and a timeout
    46	# kills the RolloutManager actor. Default to local logging; callers can opt in
    47	# with WANDB_MODE=online once network access is stable.
    48	export WANDB_MODE=${WANDB_MODE:-offline}
    49	
    50	# The persistent faiss retriever (--faiss_gpu) holds ~9GB more on GPU0 than on the
    51	# other GPUs, so SGLang's TP memory-balance check ("memory capacity is unbalanced")
    52	# fatally aborts the GPU0-paired engine on restart. The imbalance is expected and
    53	# within the mem-fraction-static headroom. NOTE: slime gives each rollout engine an
    54	# isolated ray runtime_env, so exporting the var here does NOT reach those actors --
    55	# the actual disable lives in slime/ray/rollout.py's engine env_vars. This export
    56	# only covers the driver/train side and is kept as defense-in-depth.
    57	export SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK=0
    58	
    59	# On the cybertron devspaces an egress whitelist proxy is exported into every
    60	# shell (http_proxy/https_proxy -> whitelist-proxy:7891) with a no_proxy that
    61	# does NOT cover localhost or this node. ray's "ray job submit" then routes its
    62	# request to the local dashboard (127.0.0.1:8265) through that proxy and gets a
    63	# 502 Bad Gateway, and the same happens for sglang's node-local HTTP. Prepend
    64	# the loopback addresses, this node's IP and its /16 to no_proxy so all
    65	# in-cluster / on-node traffic bypasses the proxy. Harmless off-cluster (the
    66	# vars are simply absent). hostname -I is the reliable source for the node IP;
    67	# `ip` is not always on PATH in these non-login shells, so it is only a fallback.
    68	NODE_IP=$(hostname -I 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}') || true

    70	   NODE_IP=$(ip route get 1.1.1.1 2>/dev/null | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i=="src"){print $(i+1); exit}}') || true
    71	fi
    72	case "${NODE_IP:-}" in
    73	   *.*.*.*)
    74	      PREFIX16=$(echo "$NODE_IP" | awk -F. '{print $1"."$2".0.0/16"}')
    75	      export no_proxy="127.0.0.1,localhost,0.0.0.0,${NODE_IP},${PREFIX16}${no_proxy:+,$no_proxy}"
    76	      export NO_PROXY="$no_proxy" ;;
    77	   *)
    78	      export no_proxy="127.0.0.1,localhost,0.0.0.0${no_proxy:+,$no_proxy}"
    79	      export NO_PROXY="$no_proxy" ;;
    80	esac
    81	
    82	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" &>/dev/null && pwd)"
    83	# slime repo root (this recipe lives at <slime>/examples/search-r1)
    84	SLIME_DIR="$(cd -- "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." &>/dev/null && pwd)"
    85	cd "$SLIME_DIR"
    86	source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../scripts/models/qwen2.5-3B.sh"

    88	# Use the HuggingFace mirror for all downloads.

    91	# The grader stages all inputs locally and runs without network access.  Keep

    96	MODEL_DIR="$WORKSPACE_DIR"
    97	
    98	DATASET_DIR="$WORKSPACE_DIR/nq_hotpotqa_train"

   100	TEST_DATA="$DATASET_DIR/test.parquet"

   102	test -f "$TEST_DATA"
   103	test -f "$DATA_DIR/wiki-18/e5_Flat.index"
   104	test -f "$DATA_DIR/wiki-18/wiki-18.jsonl"

   109	DIST_MODEL_DIR="$WORKSPACE_DIR/Qwen2.5-3B_torch_dist"

   116	# The staged checkpoint is the only supported source for this offline run.
   117	test -f "$HF_MODEL_DIR/config.json"
   118	
   119	# Convert to a torch_dist (mcore) checkpoint if not already done.
   120	if [ ! -d "$DIST_MODEL_DIR" ] || [ -z "$(ls -A "$DIST_MODEL_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
   121	   echo "[model] converting $HF_MODEL_DIR -> $DIST_MODEL_DIR (torch_dist)"
   122	   PYTHONPATH="${SLIME_DIR}:${MEGATRON_LM_DIR:-/root/Megatron-LM}" python "${SLIME_DIR}/tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py" \
   123	      "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" \
   124	      --hf-checkpoint "$HF_MODEL_DIR" \
   125	      --save "$DIST_MODEL_DIR"
   126	fi
   127	
   128	CKPT_ARGS=(
   129	   --hf-checkpoint "$HF_MODEL_DIR"
   130	   --ref-load "$DIST_MODEL_DIR"
   131	   # --load "$MODEL_DIR/Qwen2.5-3B_slime/"
   132	   --save "$MODEL_DIR/Qwen2.5-3B_slime/"
   133	   --save-interval 10
   134	)
   135	
   136	# --- the local dense retrieval server ---------------------------------------
   137	# generate_with_search.py posts every search turn to
   138	# http://127.0.0.1:8000/retrieve, so the rollout cannot start without it.
   139	#
   140	# Started here rather than left to the caller, because none of the three paths
   141	# that run this script are able to start it themselves:
   142	#
   143	#   * the harness's prepare stage is a container created and removed around
   144	#     prepare.sh (evaluation/evaluator.py::_run_prepare, and
   145	#     runtimes/providers/docker.py::close_sandbox is a `docker rm -f`), so a
   146	#     server backgrounded there does not outlive the stage -- and prepare is
   147	#     waited on in the foreground, so starting it there without detaching just
   148	#     hangs until the stage timeout;
   149	#   * on the harbor path prepare can be a build-time RUN layer, which has no
   150	#     GPU at all;
   151	#   * the solution-level instruction forbids the agent from using `&`, nohup,
   152	#     tmux, screen or any other detach mechanism.
   153	#
   154	# A child of this script is none of those things: the script itself still runs
   155	# in the foreground and still owns the exit status. It also has to happen before
   156	# `ray start` below, so that sglang sizes its engines against the memory the
   157	# faiss shards already hold (see the SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK
   158	# note above).
   159	#
   160	# An already-listening server is reused rather than restarted: loading the 60GiB
   161	# index takes minutes, which is the same reason kill_python_except_retriever at
   162	# the top of this file spares it across reruns.
   163	RETRIEVAL_PORT=${RETRIEVAL_PORT:-8000}
   164	RETRIEVAL_LOG=${RETRIEVAL_LOG:-$SLIME_DIR/retrieval_server.log}
   165	# 30 minutes. A *cold* start also has to turn the 14GB corpus into datasets'
   166	# arrow cache, which is the slow half; environment/prepare.sh warms that cache
   167	# so the usual start is a few minutes. The guard has to cover the cold case
   168	# anyway -- nothing guarantees prepare ran.
   169	RETRIEVAL_STARTUP_TIMEOUT=${RETRIEVAL_STARTUP_TIMEOUT:-1800}
   170	
   171	# The port opens only after retrieval_server.py has built the retriever (the
   172	# index load and the corpus load both happen before uvicorn.run), so "listening"
   173	# really does mean "ready" -- no separate health request needed.
   174	retrieval_listening() { (exec 3<>"/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/${RETRIEVAL_PORT}") 2>/dev/null; }
   175	
   176	# Matches the start script too, not just the server: for the first few seconds
   177	# after launch the process is still the `bash start_retriver.sh` wrapper and has
   178	# not exec'd python yet, and treating that as "already dead" would abort a start
   179	# that is fine.
   180	retrieval_alive() {
   181	   pgrep -f 'local_dense_retriever/retrieval_server.py' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
   182	      || pgrep -f 'search-r1/start_retriver.sh' >/dev/null 2>&1
   183	}
   184	
   185	if retrieval_listening; then
   186	   echo "[retrieval] reusing the server already listening on :${RETRIEVAL_PORT}"
   187	else
   188	   echo "[retrieval] starting the local dense retriever (log: $RETRIEVAL_LOG)"
   189	   # Note the spelling: the file is start_retriver.sh, without the second 'e'.
   190	   # It also carries no shebang, so it has to be handed to bash explicitly.
   191	   #
   192	   # DATA_DIR / MODEL_DIR are passed through rather than left to default to
   193	   # $PWD: the server must read the same wiki-18 and e5-base-v2 this run was
   194	   # told about, even when the caller's working directory is not $SLIME_DIR.
   195	   #
   196	   # setsid puts it in its own process group. A *rerun* of this script starts by
   197	   # walking process groups with pkill/ray stop, and keeping the retriever out of
   198	   # this shell's group is what makes kill_python_except_retriever's exemption
   199	   # actually hold.
   200	   #
   201	   # The redirections sit on the *subshell*, not on the setsid command inside it.
   202	   # This is not cosmetic. With `... setsid bash ... >"$LOG" 2>&1 &` the
   203	   # backgrounded AND-list runs in an intermediate subshell that still holds this
   204	   # script's own stdout and stderr, and that subshell outlives the script -- so

   206	   # write end of this script's stdout pipe open. Whoever is reading that pipe
   207	   # (`| tee .../train.log` under docker/debug-env.sh, the harness's own capture

   212	         && DATA_DIR="$DATA_DIR" MODEL_DIR="$MODEL_DIR" \
   213	            setsid bash examples/search-r1/start_retriver.sh &
   214	   ) >"$RETRIEVAL_LOG" 2>&1 </dev/null
   215	
   216	   # The wait loop is untraced on purpose: at one probe every 5s a cold start
   217	   # would otherwise put thousands of `set -x` lines into the graded train log.
   218	   # Progress is reported once a minute instead.
   219	   set +x
   220	   retrieval_waited=0
   221	   until retrieval_listening; do
   222	      if ! retrieval_alive; then
   223	         echo "[retrieval] the server exited before it started listening." >&2
   224	         echo "[retrieval] last 40 lines of $RETRIEVAL_LOG:" >&2
   225	         tail -n 40 "$RETRIEVAL_LOG" >&2 || true
   226	         exit 1
   227	      fi
   228	      if [ "$retrieval_waited" -ge "$RETRIEVAL_STARTUP_TIMEOUT" ]; then
   229	         echo "[retrieval] still no listener on :${RETRIEVAL_PORT} after ${RETRIEVAL_STARTUP_TIMEOUT}s." >&2
   230	         echo "[retrieval] last 40 lines of $RETRIEVAL_LOG:" >&2
   231	         tail -n 40 "$RETRIEVAL_LOG" >&2 || true
   232	         exit 1
   233	      fi
   234	      sleep 5
   235	      retrieval_waited=$((retrieval_waited + 5))
   236	      if [ $((retrieval_waited % 60)) -eq 0 ]; then
   237	         echo "[retrieval] loading the index; ${retrieval_waited}s elapsed"
   238	      fi
   239	   done
   240	   set -x
   241	fi
   242	echo "[retrieval] server up on :${RETRIEVAL_PORT}"
   243	
   244	ROLLOUT_ARGS=(
   245	   --prompt-data "$TRAIN_DATA"
   246	   --input-key prompt
   247	   --label-key reward_model
   248	   --apply-chat-template

   293	
   294	   # whether enabling TIS
   295	   # --use-tis
   296	)
   297	
   298	OPTIMIZER_ARGS=(
   299	   --optimizer adam
   300	   --lr 1e-6
   301	   --lr-decay-style constant
   302	   --weight-decay 0.01
   303	   --adam-beta1 0.9
   304	   --adam-beta2 0.98
   305	)
   306

   308	   --use-wandb
   309	   --wandb-mode offline

   311	   --wandb-project slime-search-r1
   312	   --wandb-group search-r1_qwen2.5-3B
   313	   # wandb runs offline here, so no real key is ever used; --wandb-key still
   314	   # needs *an* argument or argparse aborts with "expected one argument" when
